drug_class: Opioid pain reliever combined with a non-opioid pain reliever
purpose: This medication is used to relieve moderate to moderately severe pain, such as pain after surgery, injury, or dental procedures. It combines two different pain-relieving medicines that work together to give you better relief than either one alone.
how_it_works: The hydrocodone part is an opioid that works by attaching to special receptors in your brain and spinal cord, basically telling your body to feel less pain. The acetaminophen part (the same ingredient in Tylenol) helps reduce pain and fever through a different pathway. Together, they tackle your pain from two different angles, making the combination more effective.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, constipation, lightheadedness, and headache are the most common side effects. Many people also feel a little foggy or have trouble concentrating while taking this medicine.
warnings: This medicine can be habit-forming, so only take it exactly as prescribed and never share it with others. Do not drink alcohol while taking it, as this can be very dangerous. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Do not take other products containing acetaminophen (like Tylenol or cold medicines) at the same time, as too much acetaminophen can seriously damage your liver. Tell your doctor right away if you have slow or difficult breathing.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one or two tablets every four to six hours as needed for pain, but always follow exactly what your doctor prescribed. Do not take more than prescribed, and do not take it more often than directed. Your doctor will give you the lowest effective dose for the shortest time needed.
